paper.title: Learning Superconductivity from Ordered and Disordered Material Structures
paper.research_summary: The paper introduces SuperCon3D, a new dataset containing both 3D crystal structures (ordered and disordered) and experimental superconducting transition temperatures (Tc), and proposes two deep learning models—SODNet for screening known structures and DiffCSP-SC for generating novel high-Tc superconductors. It validates both models via computational (e.g., DFT) and interpretability analyses, and reports candidate materials for experimental validation.

task.objective: Design novel superconducting candidates with high Tc values
output_goal: novel crystal structures predicted to have high Tc

evidence.text: In this study, we define the design of novel superconducting candidates in two ways: the first is “known materials repurposing", where the potential superconducting candidates are screened from known structures. And the second involves designing novel material structures that are potential superconducting candidates.
Inverse Superconductor Generation Task. This task predicts the chemical composition A, the Cartesian coordinates X, and the lattice matrix L targeted on higher Tc values.

stages.stage_goal: Collect and match experimental crystal structures with experimental Tc values
stage_output: SuperCon3D dataset: 1,578 entries with both crystal structure and experimental Tc

evidence.text: We extracted approximately 33,000 superconductors with their chemical formulas and corresponding critical temperatures from SuperCon. After removing duplicates and non-superconductors, we identified 11,949 superconducting materials. Additionally, over 200,000 ordered and disordered crystal structures were gathered from the ICSD database [3]. We then matched these 11,949 SuperCon entries with 208,425 ICSD entries based on chemical composition, space group and lattice parameter. Moreover, Tc values and structural data for hydrogen-enriched superconductors were collated from various literature sources. This process resulted in 1,578 superconductor data entries, each featuring both Tc and crystal structure.

stages.stage_goal: Train an SE(3)-equivariant graph attention model to predict Tc from crystal structures (ordered and disordered)

evidence.text: Based on SuperCon3D, we propose two deep learning methods for designing high Tc superconductors. The first is SODNet, a novel equivariant graph attention model for screening known structures, which differs from existing models in incorporating both ordered and disordered geometric content.

stages.stage_goal: Train a transformer-based equivariant diffusion model to generate crystal structures conditioned on high Tc
stage_input: pre-training dataset (1.14M crystals from Materials Project, OQMD, ICSD, Matgen)

evidence.text: Additionally, we introduce DiffCSP-SC, a transformer-based equivariant diffusion model for inverse design, capable of generating novel high Tc superconductor candidates.
Based on DiffCSP [27], we further equip our method with superconductivity guidance for crystal generation. [...] We extend DiffCSP with a more powerful architecture for SuperCon3D dataset.

Considering the SuperCon3D dataset’s limited structures, which doesn’t fully capture the diversity in atomic species, lattice parameters, and atomic spatial distributions, we pre-trained our model on approximately 1.14 million unique 3D crystals sourced from existing databases, including Materials Project, OQMD, ICSD and Matgen.

stages.stage_name_raw: generating novel crystal structures with DiffCSP-SC
stages.stage_goal: Use DiffCSP-SC to sample novel crystal structures targeting high Tc

evidence.text: Utilizing our model, we aimed to generate novel superconductor candidates with high Tc values. Table 12 and 13 in Appendix E.4 displays 32 potential high Tc superconducting materials categorized as cuprate, H-rich, heavy-Fermion, iron-based, and other types.

stages.stage_goal: Apply trained SODNet to rank known ICSD structures by predicted Tc and select top candidates

evidence.text: Using our model, we screened the ICSD database to identify potential high-Tc superconductors. Appendix E.2 lists 27 candidates, including cuprate, H-rich, heavy-Fermion, iron-based, and other types. The top three candidates are Ba1.1432Co0.1429O3.0009Rh0.8574, ErH3, and Ba0.515Ca0.485, previously unreported.

stages.stage_goal: Validate electronic structure signatures of superconductivity (e.g., Van Hove singularities, flat bands) in generated/screened candidates
stage_output: DFT-verified electronic structures (band structures, DOS) showing VHS/flat bands

evidence.text: Subsequently, density-functional theory (DFT) were performed on selected candidates to verify their superconducting properties. Notably, Van Hove singularities (VHS) were observed in the electronic structures of Ba2CuCl2O2, Lu, and BaFe2Se2, as further detailed in Appendix E.5.

We conduct DFT calculation using the Vienna ab initio package (VASP) [57, 7]. The structures are fully relaxed using the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) [41] of the SCAN meta-GGA functional, employing the pseudopotentials of the projector augmented wave (PAW) method [4].

stages.stage_name_raw: wet lab synthesis and Tc characterization
stages.stage_goal: Synthesize top candidates experimentally and measure their actual Tc to close the R&D loop
stage_output: experimentally measured Tc values added to SuperCon3D

evidence.text: Fig. 8 presents a pipeline for designing SC., validating our dataset and models for real-world scenarios. We initially generate potential, ordered superconducting structures using the DiffCSP-SC model trained on the SuperCon3D database. Candidate materials are selected based on Tc values predicted by SODNet, followed by DFT verification to confirm the presence of superconducting electronic structures, such as VHS. Subsequently, selected candidates undergo wet lab synthesis, with Tc values characterized and recorded in the SuperCon3D database.
evidence.section: F Pipeline for Designing Real-world Superconductors.
